name: Scribe
overview: The role of the scribe in Scripture encompasses a variety of important duties related to the administration and preservation of God's law and the affairs of the kingdom. As shown in passages like 2 Samuel 8:17 and 1 Kings 4:3, scribes served as secretaries and recorders, responsible for documenting events and managing official records. Their responsibilities extended to financial oversight and practical management, as seen in 2 Kings 12:10-12, where the king's scribe handled temple funds and supervised their use in repairs. These verses reveal the scribe as an essential figure in both religious and civil governance, entrusted with careful stewardship and detailed record-keeping.
